name: Pig
description: Pig is a chaotic, high-energy reaction game that turns a standard deck of cards into a test of observation and speed. Played without turns, players rapidly pass cards in a circle to collect a four-of-a-kind. The game's defining feature is the 'Stupid Pose': as soon as one player completes their set and discreetly touches their nose, everyone else must follow suit. The last person to react is the 'Pig' and loses the round. It is a close relative of the game 'Spoons'.

overview.description: Pig is a chaotic, high-energy reaction game that turns a standard deck of cards into a test of observation and speed. Played without turns, players rapidly pass cards in a circle to collect a four-of-a-kind. The game's defining feature is the 'Stupid Pose': as soon as one player completes their set and discreetly touches their nose, everyone else must follow suit. The last person to react is the 'Pig' and loses the round. It is a close relative of the game 'Spoons'.

history.origins: Derived from traditional Victorian-era children's games. It evolved into a popular parlor game alongside 'Spoons' in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1890s: Games like 'Nosey Parker' and 'Snip-Snap-Snorum' introduce the collection mechanic.
1940s: 'Pig' becomes a standard summer camp and dormitory game in the US and UK.
1990s: Rebranded commercially in various 'Grab' and 'Reaction' card sets.
Present: A staple ICE-breaker and party game universally known under names like 'Donkey' or 'Spoons'.
history.cultural: Used as a metaphor for the 'Bandwagon Effect' in social psychologyâ€”people follow a leader often without knowing why the leader started.
history.evolution: The card-passing mechanic shifted from turn-based to simultaneous play to create the 'Speed-Chaos' effect that defines the modern game.

setup.players: Large groups are better (5-8 is ideal).
setup.deck: Use exactly 4 cards of the same rank for each player (e.g., if 4 players, use 4 Aces, 4 Kings, 4 Queens, 4 Jacks).
setup.dealing: Shuffle the 4-per-player set and deal 4 cards to each person.

rules.objective: Collect four cards of the same rank and be quick to react to others' completion.
rules.gameplay: All players sit in a circle with four cards each. Everyone simultaneously passes one card face down to the left and picks up the card from the right. There are no turns; passing continues as fast as players wish. You must pass one card before picking up the next; you may never hold more than four cards. When a player collects four of a kind they quietly touch their nose. As soon as one player touches their nose, all others may do the same. The last player to touch their nose loses the round (is the Pig).
keyRules: Pass one card at a time to your left; never hold more than four cards.
First to collect four of a kind touches nose; others immediately do the same.
Last to touch nose loses (the Pig).
Play is simultaneous with no turns.

strategy.basic: Don't blink! The cards are moving so fast that beginners often get 'Tunnel Vision' looking at their own hand. Your peripheral vision is your greatest assetâ€”watch the person directly across from you, not just your cards. If you see them freeze or reach for their face, react immediately even if you don't know who has the set.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Slow Pass': If you have 3 cards of a rank, you only need one more. Stop passing quickly. Wait for the person to your right to drop a card. This allows you to focus 100% on other players' faces. If you rush the pass, you might miss the subtle finger-to-nose movement of the winner.
strategy.advanced: The 'Fake-Out': If you are playing with veterans, try scratching your nose or adjusting your glasses. This often triggers a 'Panic Reaction' where everyone touches their noses. You get to laugh at them for being jumpy, and it masks your real win later in the round. Subtlety is the difference between a pro Pig player and a loser.
tips: If you are the one who completed the 4-of-a-kind, try to wait 2 or 3 seconds before touching your nose. Let the panic of the passing cards build first.
If playing the 'Spoons' variation, grab the spoon softly. The sound of a clattering spoon ruins the surprise.

variations.name: Pig with no stock pile
variations.description: Use four cards of one rank per player (e.g. 7 players use 28 cards). Shuffle and deal four each. All pass simultaneously to the left until someone has four of a kind.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine as base Pig; no engine overrides needed.

variations.name: Pig with a stock pile
variations.description: Full 52-card pack; four dealt to each player; remainder is stock to dealer's right. Dealer draws from stock; player to dealer's right discards to a pile. When stock is exhausted the discard pile becomes the new stock. Same nose-touch end.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine as base Pig; no engine overrides needed.

variations.name: Spoons
variations.description: Same passing and four-of-a-kind aim, but one fewer spoon than players in the centre. First to get four of a kind takes a spoon; then everyone may grab a spoon. Player left without a spoon loses.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine as base Pig; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: No points; each round has one loser (the Pig). Often played with three lives (letters P-I-G) or elimination until two remain.
scoring.winCondition: First to collect four of a kind and touch nose wins the round; last to touch nose loses and is the Pig.
